verdict.label: contradictory
verdict.rationale: Both abstracts report an association between circulating adiponectin and LDL cholesterol in comparable metabolic-disease populations using unadjusted correlation analysis, but in opposite directions. Study A (173 patients with type-2 DM) found a positive correlation between adiponectin and LDL (r = 0.30, P = 0.001 overall; r = 0.34, P = 0.026 in patients with at least 3 MetS components), while study B (180 individuals including MetS patients and controls) reported that adiponectin levels were negatively associated with LDL. The populations differ (type-2 DM vs MetS/controls), but both concern dysmetabolic individuals and the same exposure-outcome pair with the same contrast type, so the findings are comparable and genuinely opposite. No concrete text-supported difference (e.g., adjustment, assay, or population definition) is offered by either abstract to explain the reversal.

source_evidence.quote: We found a positive correlation between adiponectin and total cholesterol (r = 0.27, P = 0.055), LDL (r = 0.34, P = 0.026) and SD-LDL (r = 0.41, P = 0.006) in patients with at least 3 components of MetS criteria.

Adiponectin was negatively correlated with waist circumference (r = -0.16, P = 0.06) and positively with HbA1c (r = 0.19, P = 0.032), total cholesterol (r = 0.23, P = 0.017), LDL (r = 0.30, P = 0.001), SD-LDL (r = 0.41, P < 0.001), and SD-LDL/LDL (r = 0.22, P = 0.023).
Adiponectin levels were negatively associated with waist circumference, waist-hip ratio, PTX-3 and LDL.

diagnostics.notes: Extraction verified: side A correctly extracts the positive adiponectin–LDL correlation (r = 0.34, P = 0.026 in the ≥3 MetS subgroup; r = 0.30, P = 0.001 overall) with '+' direction; side B correctly extracts the negative adiponectin–LDL association with '-' direction. Both are directional association claims from correlation analyses without reported adjustment. The exposure (adiponectin) and outcome (LDL) match; the contrast type (association) matches. Populations differ (type-2 DM vs MetS/controls) but both are dysmetabolic and the abstracts do not provide a text-supported explanation for the opposite directions, so contradictory with factor none is appropriate.
